paragraphs: City Detect sells a camera and software service that helps municipalities and counties find and address urban blight before complaints pile up. Cameras ride on a city's existing fleet vehicles and collect images of properties as those vehicles drive their normal routes. The company's PASS AI then detects and maps signs of urban blight and decay from the public right of way.

Roof-mounted data collection units capture street-level imagery during routine city operations. Once the images are processed, each detection is assigned a severity score from 1 to 4 and placed on an interactive map. The conditions it picks up run to illegal dumping, tire accumulations, snipe signs, and graffiti. Staff can export timestamped, image-backed reports in a few clicks.

The company says it was founded in 2021. One published case study describes Cathedral City partnering with City Detect in June 2025. For each municipality the company performs local calibration meant to cut false-positive detections and match local rules.
